title: Roger Griswold, Connecticut's 7th governor, and the cane on the House floor
text: In 1798 a Yale man named Roger Griswold took a cane to a congressman on the floor of the House. In 1811 Connecticut made him governor. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

title: James Fenner, Rhode Island's 7th, 11th and 17th governor
text: James Fenner was governor of Rhode Island three times, so he is the state's 7th, 11th and 17th. His last stint began right after the Dorr Rebellion, the 1842 fight over who got to vote. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

title: Joseph C. Yates, New York's 7th governor, and the vote in 1821
text: Joseph C. Yates of Schenectady was the first governor elected under New York's 1821 constitution, which opened the polls to working white men and shut out nearly all Black men. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

title: James Sullivan, Massachusetts' 7th governor, taught himself the law
text: No college. Self-taught at home after a childhood injury. James Sullivan became Massachusetts' 7th governor in Harvard's backyard. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

title: William Plumer, New Hampshire's 7th governor, and the fight over Dartmouth
text: A Baptist lay preacher turned lawyer, William Plumer was governor when New Hampshire tried to turn Dartmouth into a state university. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

title: Mahlon Dickerson, New Jersey's 7th governor, went to Russia and got the Navy
text: Andrew Jackson named Mahlon Dickerson minister to Russia. He got to Washington and found out he was Secretary of the Navy instead. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.

title: George Wolf, Pennsylvania's 7th governor, and the free schools
text: George Wolf pushed Pennsylvania's free school law through in 1834, the same year a race riot tore through Philadelphia. Seven facts in a minute, from our new film Lucky Seven.
